relations.evidence: To do so, select the "store" option checkbox in the field mapping definition for the desired fields. The FTS index will store the original field contents intact (without applying any text analysis) as a part of its internal storage.

relations.subject: fts:fts-supported-queries-boosting-the-score-query
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate for a query type's literal syntax pattern
relations.evidence: Experiment with boost to adjust this. For example, a query like "name:margaret^2 hobby:singing" would give twice as much weight to a match in the name field as the hobby field.

relations.subject: search:dynamic-mapping
relations.object: true (FTS tries to index all fields in a document by default)
relations.evidence: By default, FTS tries to index all the fields in a document yet you typically only need to search on a few key fields.

relations.subject: fts:fts-supported-queries-conjuncts-disjuncts
relations.evidence: Using conjunction (AND) queries can help make the search faster. In a query string, you can do this by using the + operator (MUST).

relations.subject: search:wordlist
relations.object: excludes high-frequency terms from the index to speed up querying
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate for a wordlist's operational performance effect
relations.evidence: If possible, consider adding high frequency terms to a stop word list and reindex so they are not excluded from the index altogether.

notable_absence.finding: The page states 'FTS does not support in-memory search indexes. The search indexes are persisted to disk and are accessed as memory-mapped files' as a flat architectural fact (not a configurable setting), so it doesn't fit hasDefaultValue's subject shape; recorded here rather than forced into a relation. Similarly, the detailed tf-idf scoreFn formula (coord/tw/queryWeight/fieldWeight/idf functions) is real, precise mathematical content with no home in this schema's concept/relation shape - it belongs to search:scoring-algorithm-enum's tf-idf member but the schema has no way to attach a formula to an enum member, so only the qualitative fact (bleve uses a modified tf-idf) was captured as a relation.

cross_component_finding: This page's scoring FAQ ('FTS's internal text indexing library (bleve) uses a slightly modified version of standard tf-idf scoring... The search scoring happens at query time') describes tf-idf as THE Search Service scoring mechanism, unconditionally - it never mentions bm25 or an index-level choice between algorithms at all. This is consistent with search:scoring-algorithm-enum's own description ('tf-idf: the prior default') but reads as PRE-8.0 content that was never updated when the 8.0 bm25 option (search:scoring-model) was introduced elsewhere in the docs (server/8.0/search/set-advanced-settings.md, round 22). Not a contradiction - tf-idf genuinely is still bleve's default/legacy algorithm - but this page is silent about the choice that now exists, which is exactly the kind of staleness the round context predicted for fts-scoring.md (a page not in this batch); fts-troubleshooting.md turns out to have the same staleness independently. Also notable: the page's own 'sort field' FAQ discusses the SEARCH SERVICE's response object, not the Query service's n1ql:query-response-object - minted fts:search-response-object as a deliberately separate concept per the round context's near-miss warning #3, rather than merging the two response envelopes.
